disclosure: Voice clips are AI-generated character performances.

npc.elder-rowan.line-1.text: The little ones are not attacking. They are frightened, and fear borrows claws when nobody listens.

npc.elder-rowan.line-2.text: Three old bellstones have gone quiet beyond this clearing. If you wake them in the wrong order, the hush in the thickets folds tighter.

npc.elder-rowan.line-3.text: Begin where roots remember. The Heartroot bellstone must hear a trusted companion before any other note will answer.

npc.miri-brookscribe.line-1.text: I write down every rustle twice: once for what happened, and once for what the creature thought happened.

npc.miri-brookscribe.line-2.text: If a Mosskit trusts you, watch how its ears turn. It hears safe paths before the map admits they exist.

npc.miri-brookscribe.line-3.text: My second note is always water. Root first, brook second; that pattern keeps appearing beside every closed thicket.

npc.sable-mender.line-1.text: No bites today, only bruised feelings and burrs under the paws. I can work with that.

npc.sable-mender.line-2.text: Care moves first. Questions second. That order keeps everyone alive long enough to answer.

npc.sable-mender.line-3.text: The burrs on the rescued animals are tied in little knots. Not snares, exactly. Wards that forgot what they were protecting.

npc.lio-lantern.line-1.text: I mark the places where the light turns greenish-gold. Those are usually glades trying to be found.

npc.lio-lantern.line-2.text: Your party has to stay in one view. The woods split lonely people into stories that do not end well.

npc.lio-lantern.line-3.text: Lanterns go last. If root and brook are awake, the Lantern bellstone should point toward whoever tied the hush-knots.

npc.talla-knotwise.line-1.text: The map is not wrong. It is shy. It shows what the party is brave enough to ask about.

npc.talla-knotwise.line-2.text: Open the survey when the trail feels circular. Bellstones, NPCs, and frightened glades leave different marks.

npc.talla-knotwise.line-3.text: A folded trail can still be read: root, brook, lantern. Then look for the hand that folded it.

npc.brin-oathleaf.line-1.text: I only wanted the grove to hide from people who take more than they need.

npc.brin-oathleaf.line-2.text: The hush-knots were supposed to close empty paths. Then the animals panicked, and the knots started listening to fear.

npc.brin-oathleaf.line-3.text: If the three bellstones wake together, I can show you the first knot I tied.
